national_raw_news.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman Calls for Stronger Cybersecurity Amid Global Uncertainties
national_raw_news.content: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has urged financial sector regulators and other stakeholders to expedite the refund of unclaimed assets to their rightful owners. These include bank deposits, dividends, shares, post office savings, insurance proceeds and pension funds. Ms Sitharaman stated this while chairing the 30th meeting of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) in New Delhi yesterday. Ms Sitharaman also called for simplifying Know Your Customer (KYC) procedures and strengthening cybersecurity preparedness amid rising geopolitical uncertainties. The Council reviewed efforts under the ‘Your Money, Your Right’ campaign, which aims to facilitate the return of unclaimed financial assets to their rightful owners. It urged the concerned ministries and regulators to intensify their efforts to ensure timely refunds. The Council also deliberated on issues relating to macroeconomic and financial stability, as well as the country’s preparedness to address emerging challenges. Discussions included measures to promote innovation in the fintech sector and explore the potential of tokenisation of financial assets and other real-world assets. According to the Finance Ministry, the meeting also reviewed the country’s preparedness to protect critical information infrastructure, strengthen the resilience of security systems and enhance cybersecurity preparedness among Regional Rural Banks. In view of growing geopolitical challenges and global uncertainties, the Finance Minister called for more frequent meetings of the Council according to a predefined schedule. The meeting was attended by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra, Chief Economic Adviser Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology S. Krishnan, and other senior officials.

national_raw_news.title: SBI Assures Customers of Safe Funds After Suspected Data Breach
national_raw_news.content: The State Bank of India (SBI) has individually notified customers whose personal data was identified in a recent suspected cyber incident, assuring them that their account balances and funds remain safe. In a statement issued yesterday, the country’s largest public sector lender said, the affected customers have been informed. The bank also advised customers to follow safe digital banking practices and remain alert to suspicious calls, messages and emails. SBI initiated a detailed investigation after receiving alerts on 16th of this month from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) about suspected customer data exposure on the dark web. A preliminary analysis of around three lakh 75 thousand records identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information. The information reportedly included names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth and residential addresses. The bank immediately activated its cyber incident response and containment measures. It also appointed an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the incident and establish the nature and extent of the suspected data exposure. SBI clarified that the incident had no material impact on its business operations, financial performance or continuity. It said its core banking services continue to function normally without disruption. The bank has urged customers never to share their one-time passwords, PINs or banking passwords with anyone and to exercise caution while responding to unsolicited communications.

national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has urged Army Commanders to closely monitor geopolitical and regional developments and remain prepared to meet future challenges. Addressing the Army Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Singh emphasized the need for a long-term strategic vision spanning the next 20 to 30 years. He called upon the Indian Army’s senior leadership to remain equally prepared to respond to immediate and emerging challenges. He stressed that strategies must be dynamic and flexible to allow timely adjustments to changing circumstances. Commending the armed forces for adapting to evolving operational requirements, the Defence Minister said, Operation Sindoor demonstrated innovative thinking, enhanced synergy and superior coordination, supported by advanced weaponry. He added that the operation sent a clear message to the world that India would not hesitate to take necessary measures to safeguard its national interests. Mr Singh called for an integrated approach to modern warfare, emphasizing that success would depend on multi-domain capabilities and seamless coordination in joint operations. The Defence Minister also highlighted that defence production reached a record one lakh 78 thousand crore rupees in the financial year 2025-26, while defence exports touched an all-time high of around 38 thousand crore rupees. On the occasion, Mr Singh released the Land Warfare Doctrine, which provides an overarching framework to prepare the Indian Army for the challenges posed by the evolving nature of warfare and future conflicts. He also unveiled the annual United Nations Journal and felicitated Indian Army personnel for their notable contributions while serving as United Nations

national_raw_news.title: India Emerges as Third-Largest Arms Exporter to Europe: Defence Secretary
national_raw_news.content: India has emerged as the third-largest exporter of arms to Europe, driven by rising demand for defence equipment under the European Union’s ‘ReArm Europe’ initiative and the expansion of the country’s domestic manufacturing sector. Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh made the remarks while talking to media persons yesterday. He said India’s defence exports have reached an all-time high of 38 thousand 424 crore rupees, equivalent to around 3.6 billion euros. He said the increase in exports to Europe was largely driven by the growing demand for standard ammunition, artillery shells and other large- and small-calibre ammunition. Mr Singh said, country’s defence manufacturing ecosystem has witnessed significant growth over the past decade. He said the sector comprises 16 major public sector companies, around 840 large and medium-sized private enterprises, and nearly 17 thousand small enterprises, including start-ups. He added that India now exports defence equipment to more than 80 countries. The country’s defence exports range from artillery and ammunition to small arms, helmets, bulletproof jackets and other tactical equipment. Mr Singh highlighted that the government aims to ensure that 75 per cent of annual defence capital expenditure, estimated at 20 to 25 billion dollars, is spent domestically, with priority given to Indian-designed, developed and manufactured products. The Defence Secretary also noted that Indian defence manufacturers are attracting interest from international buyers, particularly in Southeast Asia, for a wide range of defence equipment, including small arms, components and artillery gun systems. The Defence Secretary said India plans to expand its participation in European defence procurement through joint ventures with European partners, while also encouraging European companies to manufacture in India under the Make in India initiative. He said greater integration of Indian and European defence supply chains will help meet international demand and strengthen cooperation.

national_raw_news.title: MEA Closely Monitors Safety of Indians Amid European Unrest
national_raw_news.content: India has advised its nationals in France, Italy and other parts of Europe to remain vigilant and exercise caution amid protests and unrest in several countries. The External Affairs Ministry said, Indian missions in France, Italy and Belgium are closely monitoring the situation and maintaining regular contact with members of the Indian community to ensure their safety and well-being. The advisory comes amid large-scale demonstrations across parts of Europe, reportedly fuelled in part by the rising cost of living. Protests in France last week turned violent, with incidents of arson and vandalism reported in several areas. Addressing the media, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. Indian nationals had been advised to avoid areas where protests are taking place, exercise due caution while travelling and follow advisories issued by local authorities. He added that the Indian embassies in France and Italy had also issued specific advisories for Indian citizens. The Ministry reiterated that the safety and welfare of Indians abroad remain a priority. In the French city of Limoges, protesters set fire to a historic town hall, while public property and shops were also targeted. Thousands of demonstrators also took to the streets of Paris on Thursday following a weekend of clashes and widespread looting, marking one of the country’s most serious episodes of unrest in recent years.

national_raw_news.title: Asian Para Games: India sign-off with best-ever haul of 114 medals comprising 30 gold 1 hour ago 32
national_raw_news.content: The curtains will come down on the Fifth Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, today, bringing the continental sporting event to a close. Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal will be India’s flag-bearers at the closing ceremony, scheduled to begin at 2:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Both athletes secured two gold medals each in their respective disciplines. Nishad Kumar won gold in the men’s high jump and long jump in the T47 category. With this achievement, he joined para-runner Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi as one of the few Indian athletes to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games. Mona Agarwal, meanwhile, won gold in the women’s 10-metre air rifle standing SH1 event with a Games record. She followed it up with another gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a world record. India concluded its campaign with a record haul of 114 medals, including 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze after a strong final-day finish yesterday. India’s medal tally received a significant boost yesterday, with athletes from para-badminton, archery and shooting contributing to the gold medal count. For the first time at these Games, para-athletics was not India’s leading source of gold medals. The country surpassed the previous edition medal count of 108 medals comprising 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze medals, achieved at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.

national_raw_news.title: India Women Thrash Zimbabwe by Nine Wickets in First ODI 2 hours ago 19
national_raw_news.content: In Women’s Cricket, India defeated Zimbabwe by nine wickets in the first One-Day International at Vadodara last night to take a one-nil lead in the three-match series. Chasing a target of 198 runs, India cruised to victory in just 27.1 overs, with nine wickets in hand and 22.5 overs to spare. Pratika Rawal struck an unbeaten 100 off 96 balls, including 15 boundaries, to register her third century in the 50-over format. Earlier, Shree Charani returned career-best figures of four for 23 to restrict Zimbabwe. Beloved Biza was the top scorer for Zimbabwe, with 62 runs off 92 balls. Earlier, India’s bowlers restricted Zimbabwe to 197 runs in 49.5 overs after the visitors won the toss and elected to bat. Spinner Shree Charani led the attack with figures of four for 23. Kranti Gaud claimed three wickets, while vice-captain Deepti Sharma took two and Shafali Verma picked up one. Beloved Biza was Zimbabwe’s highest scorer with 62 runs. Pratika Rawal was adjudged Player of the Match. The victory marked a dominant start for the reigning ODI world champions, who returned to the format after a gap of nearly eight months. It was also Smriti Mandhana’s first ODI as India’s full-time captain. The second match of the three-match series will be played in Vadodara tomorrow at 2 PM IST.

national_raw_news.title: 19th Urban Mobility India Conference and Exhibition Inaugurated in Bhubaneswar
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs Tokhan Sahu on Friday inaugurated the 19th Urban Mobility India (UMI) Conference and Exhibition 2026 in Bhubaneswar, bringing together policymakers, urban transport experts and industry representatives to deliberate on sustainable and inclusive mobility solutions for Indian cities. The two-day conference, being held on October 23–24 at Hotel Mayfair Sanctuary, is organised by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) through the Institute of Urban Transport (India), with the support of the Government of Odisha. This year’s theme is ‘Urban Accessibility and Liveability in Digital Age’, according to a press release by the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs. Odisha Housing and Urban Development Minister Krushna Chandra Mahapatra; Chief Secretary, Odisha, Anu Garg; Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA, Satendra Singh; and Additional Chief Secretary, Housing and Urban Development Department, Odisha, Usha Padhee attended the inaugural session, along with senior officials, policymakers, transport experts and industry representatives. The conference focuses on leveraging digital technologies to improve urban accessibility, integrate transport systems and enhance quality of life. Key areas include sustainable public transport, multimodal integration, first- and last-mile connectivity, traffic congestion, emissions reduction and inclusive mobility. Addressing the gathering, Sahu said the conference had emerged as an important national platform for shaping the future of urban transport. He stressed that urban development should be measured by how safely and independently citizens, particularly women, children, senior citizens and persons with disabilities, could travel within cities. Highlighting the expansion of metro rail infrastructure under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, Sahu said India’s operational metro network had grown from 248 km in 2014 to over 1,185 km across 26 cities. Work is underway on another 998 km of metro lines, he added. He said initiatives such as the National Common Mobility Card, QR-based ticketing and PM e-Bus Sewa, alongside metro expansion, were making public transport more accessible and sustainable. He also cited Odisha’s Ama Bus services as an example of modern, technology-enabled public transport and expressed confidence that the conference would contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Singh said around 1,500 delegates from India and abroad were expected to participate in the conference. Technical sessions, round-table discussions and a research symposium will contribute to policy discussions on efficient, sustainable and high-quality urban transport, he added. Exhibition and Key Discussions Sahu inaugurated an exhibition showcasing urban transport technologies, best practices and innovative mobility solutions. Twenty-eight exhibitors, including representatives of the Odisha government, metro rail companies, public sector organisations and private entities, are participating. The first day featured a conclave, a technical session, three round-table discussions and a special session on comprehensive regional mobility planning. Discussions covered digital technologies and data governance, gender-responsive urban planning, modernisation of bus systems, intelligent transport and the use of low-emission zones to reduce pollution and improve public health. The sessions also examined the use of real-time data, artificial intelligence and integrated mobility platforms to improve traffic management, safety and transport operations. Odisha’s experience in integrating urban and regional transport services, including Ama Bus/Mo Bus and feeder services such as Ama-E ride, also featured in the deliberations. Research Symposium and Valedictory Session A total of 46 research papers have been selected through peer review for the symposium. Twenty papers will be presented, while 26 will be showcased through posters. The three best papers, selected by a jury, will receive cash awards of ₹25,000 each. The October 24 programme will cover transit-oriented development, people-centric streets, behavioural change and public communication, intelligent and secure mobility, and rail-led integrated urban development. The conference will conclude with awards for ‘Excellence/Best Practice Projects in Urban Transport’, recognising outstanding States, cities and transport organisations. Union Minister for Housing and Urban Affairs and Power Manohar Lal is scheduled to deliver the valedictory address and present the awards alongside Mahapatra. The conference will be followed by the National Urban Conclave 2026, scheduled for October 24–25 at the same venue in Bhubaneswar. -PIB Inputs

national_raw_news.title: MoS Pabitra Margherita Visits Samoa and Naoero, Strengthens Bilateral Cooperation
national_raw_news.content: Minister of State for External Affairs, and Textiles Pabitra Margherita paid an official visit to Samoa and Naoero from October 16 to 22, 2026, during which he held discussions with the leadership of both Pacific Island nations on strengthening bilateral cooperation in capacity building, digital development, climate resilience, economic engagement and parliamentary exchanges. MoU Signed to Promote Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Samoa During his visit to Samoa, Margherita was accorded a traditional ‘Ava ceremony by Prime Minister Laʻaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polātaʻivao Fosi Schmidt and members of his Cabinet. He called on the Prime Minister and discussed cooperation in capacity building, digital development, climate resilience, economic engagement and multilateral issues. Margherita and the Samoan Prime Minister also signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on the implementation of the SENESE Project. The project aims to promote the inclusion and development of children and persons with disabilities by improving access to education, healthcare and vocational training. The Prime Minister also hosted an official lunch in honour of Margherita, who interacted with members of the Indian community in Samoa. Business Interaction and Community Engagement in Auckland During his transit visit to Auckland, Margherita attended a business interaction hosted in his honour by the India New Zealand Business Council (INZBC). The event brought together representatives of the textile and fashion sectors to discuss opportunities for bilateral cooperation. New Zealand Minister for Ethnic Communities and Minister for Sport and Recreation Mark Mitchell also attended the event. Margherita participated in Durga Puja celebrations and separately interacted with members of the Indian community. Discussions with Naoero’s Leadership During his visit to Naoero, Margherita called on President David W. R. Adeang and separately met Speaker of Parliament Marcus Stephen. The discussions focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation, parliamentary exchanges and capacity building. He also interacted with alumni of the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) and Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR) programmes, as well as members of the Indian community. He acknowledged their contributions to strengthening India–Naoero relations. Cycling Initiative and Development Cooperation As part of his engagements in Naoero, Margherita flagged off a mini-cycling event organised to mark his visit under India’s Quick Impact Project (QIP), ‘Cycling for a Stronger Naoero’. The initiative aims to develop local athletes and promote health through cycling. He also visited Naoero’s public hospital and phosphate-mining sites. The visit reaffirmed India’s commitment to strengthening its partnerships with Samoa and Naoero through development cooperation, capacity building and people-to-people exchanges, including under the framework of the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC). India remains committed to working closely with Pacific Island countries in support of their national development priorities and the shared aspirations of the region.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi emphasizes youth always remains at centre of govt’s policies and initiatives
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the youth have always remained at the centre of his government’s policies and initiatives. Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that for the past 25 years, he has been serving the nation to the best of his ability as head of the government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government has introduced the National Education Policy to align the country’s education system with the needs of a New India. He added that the policy emphasises India’s rich traditions and knowledge, imparting education in mother tongue, modern science and emerging technologies. Prime Minister Modi said that all institutions must work towards the common goals of national development and scaling the country’s pride. He stressed the need to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance and involve every citizen in the resolve to build a developed India by 2047. Prime Minister said that India has brought back more than 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past twelve years. He said that the country’s cultural heritage is being restored and its cultural sites are gaining global recognition. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s cultural sites are increasingly becoming part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the three-day Sammelan has brought together over nine thousand participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951. The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.
